name: Lima
summary_text: Worse than national — the top homicide venue in the state's own data, and the site of 2025 killings. The Public Ministry's study of LGTB homicides 2012–2021 identified 84 criminal complaints, 88 victims and 72 identified perpetrators, and found 58% of the deaths occurred in six fiscal districts, led by Lima (12) and La Libertad (10), with Lima Norte among them; Lima Centro also concentrates the highest national frequency of reported crimes overall (10.0%; eleven fiscal districts hold 62%). On 24–28 August 2025 a trans woman reported missing in Independencia (northern Lima) was found dead in her own home four days later; market colleagues and relatives publicly demanded justice. On the law side, congress approved a norm in February 2025 restricting trans people's access to public bathrooms — analysed by a national human-rights institute as 'legalised discrimination' — and a 2024 rights-observatory report counted 54 LGBTI+ murders 2020–2023, with trans women most affected. Scored relative to the national score (0.36) for Peru.

sources.title: Congreso aprueba norma que atenta contra el derecho de las personas trans a usar baños públicos - Infobae
sources.claim_summary: Infobae Perú (20 February 2025): congress approves a norm that strikes against trans people's right to use public bathrooms; interviews with an LGBTIQ rights activist describing the measure as an attack on trans people's access to public space.

sources.title: Discriminación legalizada: sobre la prohibición del Congreso a personas trans para acceder a baños públicos - IDEHPUCP
sources.claim_summary: IDEHPUCP human-rights institute bulletin, 'Discriminación legalizada': analysis of congress's prohibition on trans people accessing public bathrooms, characterised as legalised discrimination with public-space consequences.

sources.title: Perú: aumentaron los crímenes de odio y las mujeres trans son las más afectadas - Agencia Presentes
sources.claim_summary: Agencia Presentes (22 July 2024): hate crimes rose — 54 LGBTI+ people were murdered 2020–2023 according to the annual report of the LGBTI+ human-rights observatory of a Peruvian university, with trans women the most affected.
